posts.title: A van full of French work jackets from Lille
posts.content: Aoife drove back from Lille with 60 bleu de travail jackets from a closing uniform supplier. About half are moleskin, the rest cotton drill. They go on the rail in batches of ten, starting this Friday.

posts.title: Mending moth nips in army flannel
posts.content: Small moth holes in wool flannel darn well with a single strand of matching wool and a lot of patience. We charge nothing extra for mending, and we note every repair in the listing.

posts.title: Why a 1950s size 14 fits like a modern 10
posts.content: UK sizing was redrawn several times after the war, and every redraw made the numbers smaller for the same body. That is why we list the label and then ignore it.

posts.title: The field jacket that came with a letter in the pocket
posts.content: A 1950s M-1943 from a house clearance in Stockport had a folded letter in the inside pocket, dated 1954. We gave the letter back to the family and kept the jacket.

posts.title: Buying day notes: what we took and what we passed on
posts.content: Forty people came up the stairs last Monday. We bought from 23 of them. Most of the no pile was high-street denim from the last ten years, which we cannot sell for more than you paid.

posts.title: Photographing flaws before anything else
posts.content: Every piece gets its flaw photos taken first, before the nice ones. It stops us forgetting, and it means the last pictures in each gallery are the honest ones.
